html:
The Niah Caves in Sarawak hold some of the oldest evidence of modern humans in Southeast Asia. In 1958 the archaeologist Tom Harrisson found a human skull there, the Deep Skull, later dated to about 40,000 years ago.

The caves were used by people for tens of thousands of years, as hunting camps and later as burial places, with painted walls and boat-shaped coffins. Swiftlets still nest there, and their nests are collected for bird's nest soup.

Niah shows that modern humans lived in the rainforests of Borneo early, long before farming. Compare Java Man and Homo floresiensis, older human relatives found in Indonesia.
